newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aussie dlr gets reprieve but no end to uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Aussie dlr gets reprieve but no end to uncertainty.

text.p: The Australian dollar made a gesture at the upside Thursday as another day passed with no rate cut, but relief was tinged with the suspicion that policy uncertainty would drag on for weeks yet.

Analysts reckoned the silence meant the bank would wait for jobs data next week and inflation and wages figures on July 23 and 24 before deciding if a fifth cut was needed. The prospect dismayed dealers since it threatened to keep the A$ aimless.
Sentiment was also tugged two ways as Moody's revised the outlook for a number of Australian states to positive, but a NAB survey showed business conditions were mixed at best in Q2.
By 4.45 pm (0645 GMT) the local dollar had made hard work of reaching US$0.7530/35 from an early US$0.7509/14 and Wednesday's late US$0.7515/20.

It did stretch as far as US$0.7553 overnight as speculators went hunting for stop loss orders but lapsed when they met heavy offers instead. Some of the latter were rumoured to originate from an Asian bank protecting a strangle option and dealers, while always sceptical of such talk, were not keen to test its veracity by chasing the currency higher.
Support was expected at US$0.7505 and there were further bulwarks at US$0.7470 and US$0.7440, this week's low.
The big event overnight was the Federal Reserve's, not unexpected, decision to leave U.S. rates unchanged after its two-day policy meeting.

This had somewhat conflicting implications for the local dollar. It was, again, a relief to bulls since a hike would have taken official U.S. rates above those here and almost certainly triggered heavy selling of the A$.
But the market also assumed the Fed's reticence made it easier for the RBA to cut rates in the next month and were on guard for a move as early as this morning.

Most analysts continue to believe these factors argue for another easing with underlying inflation heading under the RBA's 2-3 percent target band, economic growth running well below potential and unemployment stuck at unacceptably high levels.

Many expect the case to be reinforced by the three major upcoming releases, being jobs data for June on July 10, the Q2 consumer price index on July 23 and wages data the day after. If all are as subdued as the easing camp expect, the RBA could move on July 25 or after its next board meeting on August 5.
Dealers reckoned the risk would keep the A$ capped until the market was certain the year-old easing cycle had ended.
The day's only economic data were subdued enough to bring bulls down to earth after Wednesday's strong retail sales.

The NAB survey of business conditions in Q2 found trading conditions improved slightly during the second quarter of 1997, but profitability performance deteriorated a little further and there was continued job shedding.

There was some comfort from U.S. ratings agency Moody's which revised the outlook for four states to improving from stable. On wednesday it did the same for Australia's debt, citing the government's steady fiscal policy framework and the central bank's prudent monetary policy stance.
On the crosses the dollar rose to NZ$1.1149/68 from NZ$1.1081/96 and a low of 1.0820 just a couple of weeks ago.

The Kiwi has been losing ground since the RBNZ endorsed an easing last week which was then extended by the market after soft GDP data. The central bank protested the additional loosening this morning and NZ yields leapt higher, but so far with little effect on the NZ$.

The local dollar was a shade easier on the yen at 86.10/20 from 86.40/50 but steady in trade weighted terms at 57.6. It remained sharply higher at around 22.00 baht after the Thai currency was floated Wednesday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
